questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The academic level of the receiving university was a high priority to me. I chose a university renowned for the faculty which I attended, in order to better myself within my field, and challenge my academic capabilities.

Furthermore, I chose a country known for communicating well in English. In an attempt to create the best circumstances for my learning, I wanted to make sure I could adequatedly follow the teaching material through the entire exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I've picked 8, assuming this is the positive end of the scale. I thoroughly enjoyed the academic experience of partaking in the exchange, as well as the social aspect of visitng a new country, and being immersed in local culture and traditions.

The housing associated with the university was god awful, and an enormous stress factor for me while visiting. The majority of the remaining 350 residents in the building had the same issue, and while a separate company was in charge, we all expressed our disappointment with the university - as they as collaborators should have an interest in their students well being.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very clear to me. Everything needed in time for start of the academic year had been communicated to me digitally.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was really no need for further assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It wasn't particularly difficult, as the housing platform was offered to any and all exchange students who applied and paid. There were limited accomodations, so I've heard of several who did not manage to secure accomodation. 

I would NOT recommend the accomodations at Van Hasseltlaan in Delft. They are run down, lack insulation, constant daily homeless invasions, repairing the broken boiler took almost a month in October, meaning no hot water or heating in what is arguably winter, and a complete neglect and dismissive attitde in regards to the problem from the housing firm (DUWO Delft).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would strongly recommend finding housing with other students from the same university, if not faculty. It is an enormous campus, with plenty of students moving from abroad, all in need of housing. The city has a strong tradition of large scale common housing for students, where groups up to 25 people live in the same house. This I've experienced to be very socially fulfilling and safe.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was absolutely horrendous - just repeating what I expressed previously:

I would NOT recommend the accomodations at Van Hasseltlaan in Delft. They are run down, lack insulation, constant daily homeless invasions, repairing the broken boiler took almost a month in October, meaning no hot water or heating in what is arguably winter, and a complete neglect and dismissive attitde in regards to the problem from the housing firm (DUWO Delft).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
It was rather straight forward. Masters exchange students are required to participate in premade-packages within their field of study, with just one available to me. The course catalogue of the packages was readily available online, and contained course codes which could be looked up on the universitys platform. 

As an exchange student, I did not have to pick any electives or apply for course, once I had been enrolled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Plenty through email correspondence if necessary, I imagine.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Perfectly fine.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular - but submit your OLA in time, and keep track of dates with a calendar.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level was high, ambitious, future-oriented and up to speed with current times and world events.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
They strongly resembled the master's courses at my home university. The structure was almost identical, having two quarters in a semester, each quarter often consisting of a a design course, with a theory course alongside it. The theory courses would however only make up 5 ECTS points, where the Design courses took up 10 ECTS points. 

The expected amount and level of deliverables were higher than expected - meaning higher than I've been accustomed to at my home university. This is rather niché being a design-oriented master's programme, but it meant for some very, very busy final weeks for each and every course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Indeed very similar. A lot of the course teaching consisted of lectures backed up by following excersizes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AR1LA011 - Architecture and Landscape: Design Studio (10 ECTS)
AR1LA021 - Architecture and Landscape: Theory, Method and Critical Thinking (5 ECTS)
AR1LA051 - Dutch Landscape: Design Studio (10 ECTS)
AR1LA061 - Dutch Landscape: Theory, Method and Critical Thinking (5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The same courses - there simply are no other choices available to exchange students on the Landscape Architecture programme.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Some housing in the Netherlands do not include certain public services such as collection of refuse or maintenance of sewers and the waternet within the municipality. It is possible to receive surcharges for these by letter. I strongly suggest to check your contract, and subsequently contact the municipality in order to prepare and budget for these costs.

The transportation by train can become enormous quite quickly - I recommend all students to invest in the personal OV-chipcard, with a monthly weekend-free subscription. It is equivalent to one trip to Amsterdam and back, each month, and allows for tree train service all weekend, all over the Netherlands.

Some intercity trains (named Intercity Direct) require an additional ticket - it is not always apparent on the route planning apps, that you'll need one, so make sure to check the type of train as well. They aren't expensive at all, but the fine for not having one sure is.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Generally, I was surprised at how similar everything was in price to Denmark. Groceries are just about the same in my experience, with take-out being somewhat cheaper - for better or for worse.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While a lot of sports associations are present at the university, to a very impressive degree, each and every one I applied for would not accept non-Dutch speaking students, and most expected you to be an active member for at least two full university years, in order to be considered during the application process.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tonnes were arranged, however I mostly participated in private arrangements between friends from my classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is an introduction programme in place, which I particapted in myself. This was a great opportunity to meet new people, and become acquianted with the campus grounds and facilities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend most design-interested students to visit the Museumpark in Rotterdam, as well as the Nieuwe Instituut right next to it.

Otherwise, both Den Haag and Amsterdam are full of art museums, highlighting dutch painting history - these I found to be very fulfilling.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Rather easy, I must say. Denmark and the Netherlands seem strikingly similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend as many after school activities as possible, and be yourself

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found none particularly challenging - the Dutch people I met were generally open and friendly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The appreciation of bicycles in the Netherlands is unavoidable - and having a bike is really quite crucial for getting around. Luckily, there are several great opportunities for finding a used bike, or renthing on at a fair price.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Take care of the paperwork in due time
- Make sure to read the fine print
- Befriend as many people as you would allow yourself

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular - it is a well structured University with tonnes of different ways of contacting them regarding any issues that may arise. Professors are also generally friendly and helpful, so don't hesitate to ask if you're unsure - even if it is regarding non-academic issues.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Interacting with new and likeminded people from all over the world in my class was very fulfilling. I've made new friendships which I look forward to cherish for many years to come.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Overcoming the housing circumstances ended up being a real nuisance. Despite this, I thought the exchange was rather challenge free. The only real tasks apart from attending classes of course, are paperwork leading up to the exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
